Change c0257. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XIII.

Context before (unchanged): Was I then a monster, a blot upon the earth, from which all men fled, and whom all men disowned?

1818 text: "I cannot describe to you the agony that these reflections inflicted upon me; I tried to dispel them, but sorrow only increased with knowledge. Oh, that I had for ever remained in my native wood, nor known or felt beyond the sensations of hunger, thirst, and heat!

1831 text: "I cannot describe to you the agony that these reflections inflicted upon me: I tried to dispel them, but sorrow only increased with knowledge. Oh, that I had for ever remained in my native wood, nor known nor felt beyond the sensations of hunger, thirst, and heat!

Diff: " I cannot describe to you the agony that these reflections inflicted upon me [-;-] {+:+} I tried to dispel them, but sorrow only increased with knowledge. Oh, that I had for ever remained in my native wood, nor known [-or-] {+nor+} felt beyond the sensations of hunger, thirst, and heat!

Context after (unchanged): "Of what a strange nature is knowledge!

result.rationale: Semicolon changed to colon after 'upon me', and 'known or felt' becomes 'known nor felt'; both are punctuation or syntax-level adjustments that leave the meaning of the creature's lament unchanged.
